prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 is a small root-cause fix in _initialize() that computes token_expiry_time from the stored token's expires_in, and ships with a new expired_tokens test fixture exercising the scenario. #2875 is a larger workaround that inserts a stored-refresh-token attempt ('Step 3.5') into the 403/insufficient_scope branch of async_auth_flow, and its own added comment states the reason it's needed verbatim: 'A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid' -- the same defect #1784 patches at the source. Once token_expiry_time is correctly restored, the proactive validity check earlier in async_auth_flow already triggers a refresh before the request is sent, so the 401/403 path #2875 patches is no longer reached for this scenario, making its added branch redundant and untested against the root cause.

prs.title: fix(streamable-http): wait for post_writer before yielding
prs.author: Epochex
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: post_writer is spawned via tg.start_soon()/similar without signaling readiness, so the caller can begin writing to write_stream / opening the GET SSE stream before post_writer's write_stream_reader is actually being consumed, creating a race that can drop or misorder the first message(s). members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: post_writer is spawned via tg.start_soon()/similar without signaling readiness, so the caller can begin writing to write_stream / opening the GET SSE stream before post_writer's write_stream_reader is actually being consumed, creating a race that can drop or misorder the first message(s). members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: post_writer is spawned via tg.start_soon()/similar without signaling readiness, so the caller can begin writing to write_stream / opening the GET SSE stream before post_writer's write_stream_reader is actually being consumed, creating a race that can drop or misorder the first message(s). members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Pickling an MCPError subclass (concretely UrlElicitationRequiredError, tracked as issue #2431) raises TypeError on unpickle: the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data), which doesn't match UrlElicitationRequiredError's own constructor signature (elicitations, message=None). (2 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: #2478 fixes this at the MCPError base-class level via a shared _restore_mcp_error dispatcher: any subclass reconstructs through from_error_data, with UrlElicitationRequiredError special-cased to from_error to preserve the typed elicitations list — the same reconstruction path #2555 hand-rolls, but generalized so any future MCPError subclass with a custom __init__ is covered, not just this one. It also drops the `# pragma: no cover` on MCPError.data, indicating the generic path is now exercised by a round-trip test. #2555's __reduce__ is scoped to UrlElicitationRequiredError only and would need to be re-added for every other subclass that overrides __init__, so it's a narrower instance of the same fix already subsumed by #2478.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: Both patch `RequestResponder.cancel()` in src/mcp/shared/session.py to fix the same defect: the method was sending an inappropriate error response back to the peer whenever a request got cancelled. #2493 (base commit 243eef5ae6) simply deletes the 'send an error response to indicate cancellation' code path, leaving cancel() send nothing at all. #2514 is built off the identical base commit (243eef5ae6) and rewrites the same method: it imports `CancelledNotificationParams` and replaces the removed response-send with a spec-compliant `notifications/cancelled` message covering both the request-timeout and caller-cancellation trigger paths, and its diff shows a `# pragma: no cover` removed from the entry-guard line in `cancel()`, indicating new tests now exercise that method end-to-end. Since both PRs rewrite the exact same lines of the same method to solve the same root cause (cancel() must not just fire an ad-hoc error response), only one can land without a direct merge conflict.
